pathogen.value: Chicken anemia virus (Gyrovirus chickenanemia), a single-stranded DNA virus

value: passed from hen to chick through the egg
spread bird to bird through droppings (fecal-oral route)
pale comb, wattle, eyelids and legs
small skin bruises and bleeding spots
dullness, depression and difficulty moving in severe cases

mortality.value: up to 10% of chicks can die during outbreaks in young chicks

diagnosis.value: suspected from clinical signs and a low blood count (hematocrit below about 27%), confirmed by virus testing such as PCR or antibody tests; post-mortem shows shrunken immune organs, bleeding in tissues and pale watery bone marrow

value: vaccinating breeding hens to stop egg-to-chick transmission

treatment_overview.value: there is no specific treatment; infected flocks often cull sick birds, and surviving birds develop immunity

summary.value: Chicken anemia virus only infects chickens and attacks bone marrow and immune cells, causing anemia and weakened immunity mainly in young chicks under three weeks old. Visible illness is now uncommon thanks to breeder vaccination, but the virus survives well in the environment and quietly circulates in many flocks without symptoms.
